text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:

- The parliamentary board of finance and monetary politics agreed to a bill that would introduce an extra tax on new cars which would be two percent for each litre of petrol usage above five litres per 100 kilometres. If the bill gets parliamentary approval it would be enforced in July.

- City representatives of countries that hope to join the European Union as soon as possible, among them Dimitrij Rupel, mayor of Slovenia's capital of Ljubljana, started a two-day meeting in Brussels on Wednesday.
- The police have not yet found reasons for a tragic accident during a rescue exercise in the Slovenian Alps where five rescuers were killed.
- The Chamber of Commerce said outdated technology is hampering international competitiveness of Slovenian companies.
- The government Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said GDP growth was expected to rise to four percent in 1997 and 4.5 percent in 1998 from 3.1 in 1996.
- President of parliament Janez Podobnik met his German counterpart Rita Suessmuth in Bonn on Wednesday in order to debate Slovenia's bid for EU and NATO memberships.

- The parliamentary board of international relations said a memorandum on the succession of the former Yugoslavia, offered to successor states by Sir Arthur Watts, was inacceptable for Slovenia because it did not grant equality to all successors.
- The Interior Ministry said over 5,000 Slovenians were cheated by private financial companies that were promising high interest rates but ended in bankruptcy in the past couple of years.
